mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a month is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite consistent labor strength (moving average of 20-day returns < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% year-over-year growth is followed by a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in all months with INDPRO > 2% YoY growth (no out-of-sample edge).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as expectations of future disinflation support equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite sustained CPIAUCSL below 3% (over 6 months).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP exceeds 1.5%, it indicates excess liquidity in the financial system, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as rates are expected to rise.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during the liquidity condition (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) below 7 million coinciding with a steady UNRATE below 4% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to labor market cooling and reduced hiring momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 7 million while UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the identified cooling (out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.2 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a soft landing, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.2pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant during the disinflation period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) lags consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 10 percentage points, it indicates supply-side weakness and predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: 6-month MA(INDPRO) - CPIAUCSL > 10% over the same window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the supply dislocation signal (out-of-sample).
